etymologies.etymologyHTML: Origin uncertain; originally pusle. Possibly from pose (“to perplex, puzzle, interrogate”) +‎ -le (frequentative suffix). The verb (1590s) “to perplex” seems to predate the noun “state of being perplexed” (circa 1600), “perplexing question” (1650s), “toy” (1814).

definitions.definition: Anything that is difficult to understand or make sense of.
A game for one or more people that is more or less difficult to work out or complete.
(archaic) Something made with marvellous skill; something of ingenious construction.
The state of being puzzled; perplexity.
(transitive) To perplex, confuse, or mystify; to cause (someone) to be faced with a mystery, without answers or an explanation.

quote.citation: 1927, F. E. Penny, chapter 4, in Pulling the Strings:
quote.text: The case was that of a murder. It had an element of mystery about it, however, which was puzzling the authorities. A turban and loincloth soaked in blood had been found; also a staff.

quote.text: When it comes to God’s existence, I’m not an atheist and I’m not an agnostic. I’m an acrostic. The whole thing puzzles me.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To think long and carefully in bewilderment.
(transitive) To make intricate or difficult to resolve; to entangle.
